recipes.name: Ultra Easy Cream Cheese Dip
ingredients_raw: 4 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, room temperature
1 teaspoon garlic salt, or to taste

steps.text: Place cream cheese in a large bowl. Gradually pour in milk, and mash cream cheese with a fork until blended and smooth. Stir in garlic salt.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultra Easy Cream Cheese Dip
raw_recipe.description: Super simple, 3-ingredient cream cheese dip with softened cream cheese, milk, and garlic salt. This creamy dip is particularly tasty with potato chips!
raw_recipe.name: Ultra Easy Cream Cheese Dip
recipeIngredient: 4 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, room temperature
1 teaspoon garlic salt, or to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Place cream cheese in a large bowl. Gradually pour in milk, and mash cream cheese with a fork until blended and smooth. Stir in garlic salt.

review.reviewBody: My family has made a similar dip recipe for years. As a child, I would take turns with my brothers & sister to make the next batch. We used garlic & onion powder instead of the garlic salt. We also added worchestershire sauce (to taste - not too much). We usually used a couple large bricks of cream cheese & added milk until it was the desired consistancy. No measurments - everything to the taste. We mixed all with a fork, but I use my stand mixer nowadays. Way better than store bought dips!

I tweaked this.. I used about 3/4 cup skim milk.. stirring in 1/4 cup at a time. I used 2 teaspoons of onion soup mix and whisked it all together and topped with parsley. it was a hit! I will be making this again!

I split the recipe in 1/4 for a smaller group. One 8 oz brick creme cheese. NOTE: I only used 1/3 cup of milk, as I thought it was too runny to use a whole cup of milk. I used Garlic Powder instead of Garlic Salt - 1/2 Teaspoon. I added Italian Seasoning - 1 Tablespoon and added fresh chopped scallions. I left it in the fridge for a couple of hours before serving. Garnished with fresh chopped scallions before serving. It was delicious - the Ladies Group loved it! Great with crackers and veggies.

It was very easy, but it needed some more taste and color. I sparingly put in garlic salt, adding dried minced onion to taste (I really didn't want it to be too salty). Still, it was lacking something visually...I always have frozen chopped spinach on hand. Since I made this recipe for only about 8 people, I cooked up a a small amount of the frozen spinach (about a 1/4 cup, drained)...added it to the dip and big improvement. You can certainly tailor this recipe to your taste. I'll be making this again.

My family has been making this dip forever! We always use an electric mixer because its clumpy otherwise. The author says it gets "foamy," but that's not true if you soften the cream cheese and add the milk a couple of tablespoons at a time. I never measure the milk; just keep adding it until it's at the right consistency. I also use half garlic powder/half garlic salt to keep it from getting too salty. Embarrassingly difficult to stop eating when combined with potato chips!!!

I have been making a variation of this recipe for years. Instead of milk I dilute beef bouillion in water and add to, room temperature, cream cheese. Mix in a blender for a creamy consistency. Spice as desired with garlic and/or onion powder, red pepper, cumin etc.

Super quick and easy! Used garlic powder, salt and pepper, dried chives and a bit of fresh green onion. Totally delicious! It doesn’t take long to incorporate the milk into the cream cheese smoothly when you add the milk only a little at a time. Will make again

My family has been using a variation on this dip for years -- usually use garlic powder in addition to the garlic salt, and just add the milk & seasonings to your own taste/consistency. Especially fabulous (and addictive) with Fritos (Scoops or regular) and/or veggies. I usually don't make this large an amount -- one brick of cream cheese, two if I think I need a ton. The cream cheese is best if room temperature or a little warmer; I sometimes pop it in the microwave to soften, and I like to use a whisk to blend, though my brother & mother make it in a blender. I also sometimes add parsley to make it look fancier.
I used an electric beater, and added dill and onion powder. I love the simplicity and variability, but there's no way it should have that much milk. I used half and it was just right.

I have been making this recipe for years. If you soften the cream cheese first and add the milk 1/8 c. at a time, you can use the hand mixer, just beat until the foam goes away. Also if you want a little less salt intake you can substitute some or all of the garlic salt with garlic powder. It is great on hamburgers too :D !!!
Easy! I made one fourth of the recipe. I added the milk a tbsp at a time, and added real garlic cloves. Served with red and yellow bell pepper strips and cucumber slices.
Eat it but it was very wet. Could not thicken it.
I used Herbs de Provence and Sea Salt instead of garlic powder. 10/10 would recommend.
So I followed the recipe the recipe to a T and instead of dip I got soup. That is way too much milk that you were asking for. You might want to change your ratio of ingredients.

I used room temperature cream cheese, 3/4 the amount of milk and had to put it in my blender and pulse it because it was so chunky. It was also way too soupy with even the amount of milk I used so I added 3/4 cup of flour which helped thicken it up. Not much flavor.
runny....good though with garlic salt.

Delicious! I added a few drops of Worcestershire sauce and only used one brick of low-fat cream cheese and this turned out great! Honestly, I think you could use any combination of your favorite seasonings to adapt it to your tastes and your chip flavor.

I use 2 blocks cream cheese, 1/4-1/3 cup milk, 2-5 pressed garlic cloves (add min, adjust to taste after mixing). Mix with handheld mixer for 3-5 mins. I refrigerate it for at least one hour to let everything meld. Serve with thick chips wavy ruffles or lays, fritos, etc. My son and his friends ask for this almost every weekend. You can also change it up with some of the other suggestions, but this is how my son loves it.

pretty blah after making this recipe & I'll. never buy premade French Onion Dip again. Plus this recipe gets changed up with other fresh herbs only & a touch of ranch dry mix with veggies when our garden is producing fresh veggies & herbs
Old family favorite. We add finely chopped green onion however, and sometimes a little worchestershire sauce and seasoned salt. As others have said, just add the milk until right consistency.
